quickSummary: Water self-ionizes with K_w = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C. Heating increases K_w (neutral pH = 6.5 at 60°C). Polyprotic acids have K_a1 ≫ K_a2 ≫ K_a3 due to electrostatic attraction; for diprotic acids, [A²⁻] ≈ K_a2 independent of C.
summary: Master water autoprotolysis thermodynamics, temperature shifts of neutrality, and polyprotic ionization approximations.

summaryBox.title: Water Auto-Ionization
summaryBox.takeaway: K_w = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴ at 25°C. As T rises, K_w increases, neutral pH drops (< 7), but water remains neutral ([H⁺] = [OH⁻]).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
TEMPERATURE DEPENDENCE OF K_w AND NEUTRAL pH
                   
   Because auto-ionization is ENDOTHERMIC, increasing temperature INCREASES K_w:
   ├── At 25°C: K_w = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ ⟹ Neutral pH = 7.0
   └── At 60°C: K_w ≈ 1.0 × 10⁻¹³ ⟹ Neutral pH = 6.5 (Water is still neutral, [H⁺] = [OH⁻]!)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Water undergoes self-ionization (autoprotolysis):
$$\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_3\text{O}^+(aq) + \text{OH}^-(aq) \quad (\Delta H^\circ > 0, \text{ Endothermic})$$
$$\mathbf{K_w = [\text{H}^+][\text{OH}^-] = 1.0 \times 10^{-14} \text{ at } 25^\circ\text{C} \quad (\text{p}K_w = 14.0)}$$
$$\mathbf{\text{pH} + \text{pOH} = \text{p}K_w = 14.0 \quad (\text{at } 25^\circ\text{C})}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 5.2 Ionization of Polyprotic Acids (e.g., H₃PO₄, H₂S)
conceptBreakdown.title: 5.2 Ionization of Polyprotic Acids (e.g., H₃PO₄, H₂S)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Polyprotic acids possess more than one acidic hydrogen per molecule and ionize in sequential steps:
$$\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 \underset{K_{a1}}{\rightleftharpoons} \text{H}^+ + \text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^- \underset{K_{a2}}{\rightleftharpoons} \text{H}^+ + \text{HPO}_4^{2-} \underset{K_{a3}}{\rightleftharpoons} \text{H}^+ + \text{PO}_4^{3-}$$
$$\mathbf{K_{a1} \gg K_{a2} \gg K_{a3}}$$
• **Electrostatic Cause**: Removing a positively charged $\text{H}^+$ proton from a neutral molecule ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$) requires much less energy than removing $\text{H}^+$ from a negatively charged anion ($\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ or $\text{HPO}_4^{2-}$).
• **Diprotic Approximation Rule**: For a weak diprotic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{A}$) where $K_{a1} \gg K_{a2}$:
- $[\text{H}^+] \approx \sqrt{K_{a1} \cdot C}$ (governed almost exclusively by the first step).
- $[\mathbf{A^{2-}}] \approx \mathbf{K_{a2}}$ (The concentration of the divalent anion is independent of initial acid concentration!).

quickRevision: Water at 60°C has neutral pH ≈ 6.5, but is strictly neutral since [H⁺] = [OH⁻].
K_a1 ≫ K_a2 ≫ K_a3 for polyprotic acids.
For diprotic acid: [A²⁻] ≈ K_a2 (independent of concentration C).
